chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'all from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Wasi' Ali ibn al-Sarri said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Ali ibn al-Sarri has died and he bequeathed to me.' He said, 'May Allah have mercy on him.' I said, 'And indeed his son Ja'far had intercourse with his mother of a concubine, so he ordered me to remove him from the inheritance.' He said to me, 'Remove him, and if you are truthful, the 'Khabal' (a specific ailment or sign of truthfulness) will befall him.'

He said, 'So I returned and presented myself to Abu Yusuf the Judge.' He said to him, 'May Allah rectify you, I am Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Sarri, and this is my father's executor. Order him to give me my inheritance from my father.' He said to me, 'What do you say?' I said to him, 'Yes, this is Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Sarri, and I am the executor of Ali ibn al-Sarri.' He said, 'Then give him his wealth.'

So I said, 'I want to speak with you.' He said, 'Come close.' So I came close where no one would hear my speech, and I said to him, 'This one had intercourse with his father's concubine, so my father ordered me and bequeathed to me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him anything.' So I went to Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) in Medina, informed him, and asked him. He ordered me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him anything. He said, 'By Allah, did Abu al-Hasan order you?' I said, 'Yes.' He made me swear three times, then said, 'Execute what he ordered you, for his word is decisive.'
The executor said, 'Then the 'Khabal' befall him after that.' Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha said, 'I saw him after that, and the 'Khabal' had befallen him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'This ruling is confined to this specific case and is not extended to others, because it is not permissible for a man to be removed from the rightful inheritance based on the bequeather's word and command to remove him, if his lineage is established and apparent, and his birth is well-known. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:'

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَد: Mother of a concubine (a concubine who bore her master a child)
key_terms.الْخَبَل: A specific ailment or sign (used here as a confirmation of truth)

ai.seo_question: How does a specific bequest from a father override standard inheritance rights for a son in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-wasiyyah* (bequest) overriding standard inheritance shares, specifically where Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) directed the exclusion of Ja'far ibn Ali al-Sarri from his father's estate due to his act of *itqa* (freeing a concubine) or specific misconduct, predicting 'Khabal' (madness/illness) as divine confirmation. The ruling is contextual, emphasizing that a clear bequest from the deceased can disinherit a specific heir even if his lineage is established, a nuance distinct from general inheritance laws. This case highlights the practical application of Shia jurisprudence where the Imam's authority validates the execution of the bequest against the default rules of *fara'id*.
